references.text: Here Jesus proclaims that he is the good shepherd who lays down his life for the sheep, which is the direct action he refers to in 10:17 as the basis for the Father's love.
Jesus repeats the motif of laying down his life for the sheep and emphasizes that this is why the Father knows him and he knows the Father, a direct parallel to 10:17.
Jesus confirms that he has authority both to lay down his life and to take it up again, which expands on the claim in 10:17 that he lays down his life in order to take it up again.
Jesus says that he can tear down the temple and rebuild it in three days, an early hint of his authority over his own life and death, which he later explains in 10:17.
Jesus gives up his spirit, marking the moment he lays down his life, which is the prerequisite for him taking it up again later as described in 10:17.
